name: Tbilisi International Airport
before:
Georgia's busiest airport, 17 km south east of Tbilisi, handling 4.75 million passengers in 2024. Over 45 airlines fly from here to more than 25 countries, mainly across Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia.

Growth has been steep. Passenger numbers went from 1 million in 2010 to almost 4 million before the pandemic, on the back of Georgia's rise as a destination.

One political constraint shapes the route map. After a row in June 2019, Russia banned flights to and from Georgia from 8 July 2019, and the ban was still in force at the end of 2021. Georgian Airways ran Tbilisi to Moscow through Yerevan using Aircompany Armenia instead. Check the current position before quoting anything routing through Russia.

The airport is operated by TAV Airports, part of Groupe ADP, and is the hub for Georgian Airways as well as MyWay Airlines.

It was named after Shota Rustaveli, the medieval Georgian poet, by the Tbilisi City Assembly in 2015.
after:
Georgia's busiest airport, 17 km south east of central Tbilisi. It handled more than 5.4 million passengers in 2025, up 13.7 per cent on 2024. Sixty-three airlines fly from here to 71 destinations, and it is the base for Georgian Airways.

TAV Airports, part of Groupe ADP, has run the airport since 2005, when it handled about 540,000 passengers a year. A USD 150 million expansion will take capacity past 10 million passengers a year, with work due to finish as early as 2028.

Russia banned flights to and from Georgia in July 2019 after protests in Tbilisi. It lifted the ban in May 2023.

Its full name is Shota Rustaveli Tbilisi International Airport.
